synopsis: Chapter 12 and the glossary cite Buehler, Griffin and Ross’s 1994 research as evidence of systematic underestimation of completion times for academic and non-academic tasks [f9598, f16312]. In the thesis-completion study, only 29.7% of students finished by their own best-estimate date [f9599, f16311]. Underestimation persisted even under pessimistic instructions, and participants focused on their current plan rather than relevant past outcomes [f9600, f9601, f16312]. The glossary rates the planning-fallacy finding as proven; the supplied facts agree across locations but do not quantify its effects on the booklet’s validation project [f16312, f9598, f9599, f9600, f9601].
